# casdoor_syncer (Resource)

Manages a Casdoor syncer, which synchronizes the users of an organization with an external database or system.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are written to Casdoor. The other fields of the object, including the ones not listed here, keep their current values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "casdoor_syncer" "hr" {
  name          = "syncer-acme-hr"
  organization  = casdoor_organization.acme.name
  type          = "Database"
  database_type = "mysql"
  host          = "db.acme.example.com"
  port          = 3306
  user          = "casdoor"
  password      = var.hr_db_password
  database      = "hr"
  table         = "employee"
  sync_interval = 60
  is_read_only  = true
  is_enabled    = true

  table_columns = [
    {
      name         = "id"
      type         = "string"
      casdoor_name = "Id"
      is_key       = true
    },
    {
      name         = "login"
      type         = "string"
      casdoor_name = "Name"
    },
    {
      name         = "email"
      type         = "string"
      casdoor_name = "Email"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the syncer, unique within its owner.
- `organization` (String) The organization whose users are synchronized.

### Optional

- `affiliation_table` (String) The table that holds the affiliations.
- `avatar_base_url` (String) The base URL prepended to the avatars.
- `cert` (String) The name of the cert used by the SSH tunnel.
- `database` (String) The name of the database.
- `database_type` (String) The database type, e.g. `mysql`, `postgres` or `mssql`.
- `host` (String) The host of the source.
- `is_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the syncer is enabled.
- `is_read_only` (Boolean) Whether the source is only read, so that changes in Casdoor are not written back.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the source.
- `port` (Number) The port of the source.
- `ssh_host` (String) The host of the SSH tunnel.
- `ssh_password` (String, Sensitive) The password of the SSH tunnel.
- `ssh_port` (Number) The port of the SSH tunnel.
- `ssh_type` (String) How the SSH tunnel authenticates, empty when no tunnel is used.
- `ssh_user` (String) The user of the SSH tunnel.
- `ssl_mode` (String) The SSL mode of the database connection.
- `sync_interval` (Number) The number of seconds between two synchronizations.
- `table` (String) The table that holds the users.
- `table_columns` (Attributes List) How the columns of the table map to Casdoor user fields. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--table_columns))
- `type` (String) The type of the source, e.g. `Database` or `Keycloak`.
- `user` (String) The user of the source.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) The time when the syncer was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the syncer in the `owner/name` format.

<a id="nestedatt--table_columns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `table_columns`

Required:

- `name` (String) The name of the column.

Optional:

- `casdoor_name` (String) The Casdoor user field, e.g. `Name`, `DisplayName` or `Email`.
- `is_hashed` (Boolean) Whether the column is included in the hash that detects changes.
- `is_key` (Boolean) Whether the column identifies the user.
- `type` (String) The type of the column, e.g. `string`, `integer` or `boolean`.
- `values` (String) The values of the column.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the name.
terraform import casdoor_syncer.example <name>
```
